chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Huzayfa ibn Mansur, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'You know my situation, the extent of my generosity, and my willingness to provide for my brothers. So, if I accompany a group of them on the road to Mecca, I can extend my generosity upon them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not do it, O Shihab! If you extend (your generosity) and they extend (their expectations), you will burden them; and if they withhold (their share), you will humble them. Therefore, accompany your equals.'

key_terms.أَجْحَفْتَ بِهِمْ: You would burden them / Aggrieve them

ai.seo_question: Why should one avoid showing off generosity to a group of friends according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih to avoid accompanying peers of unequal financial standing to prevent the social friction of *tajannuf* (partiality) or *idhall* (humiliation). This teaching highlights the Shia ethical emphasis on *mu'asharah* (social conduct) and the psychological impact of economic disparity on dignity, urging believers to choose companionship based on equality to preserve mutual respect.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Hassan Bin Al husayn Al lulu’ie, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Huzayfa Bin Mansour, from Shihab Bin Abd Rabbih who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> have recognised my (affluent) state and the extent of my (helping) hand and my extending (favours) upon my brethren. So, can I accompany a number of them in the road to Makkah, so that I can extend (favours) upon them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Don’t do it, O Shihab! If you extend and they extend, you would aggrieve them; and if they withhold, you would (end up) humiliating them. Therefore, accompany your equals’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from al-Hassan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu’lu’iy from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur from Shihab ibn ‘Abd Rabbihi who has said the following: “

I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘You are aware of my affluent condition and my extending helping hand toward my brothers (in belief). Should I accompany certain individuals from among them during my journey to Makkah and extend a helpful hand toward them?’ He (the Imam) replied, ’You must not do so, O Shihab. If you do so, they will also do it, you overburden them, and if they did not do so, you have humiliated them. Therefore, accompany people like yourself.”’
